correctness.rationale: For F=sum_i X_i^(d-1)X_(i+1) in characteristic p|d the gradient equations reduce to X_(i-1)^(d-1)=X_i^(d-2)X_(i+1). Any geometric zero coordinate forces all zero, so the gradient scheme is wholly in the projective torus. On X_0=1, x_i=t^a_i with a_i=[1-(1-d)^i]/d; unit-coordinate elimination leaves exactly t^a_m=1 as a scheme ring equality. Multiplying gradients by coordinates shows all cyclic monomials coincide and F=m*T_0; if p does not divide m the full singular scheme is empty, while for p|m it is Spec k[t]/(t^N-1), N=|a_m|. Writing N=p^nu*N0 gives N0 reduced points with curvilinear length p^nu each. Lifting-the-exponent establishes nu=vp(m), except p=2,d=2(mod4), when nu=v2(d-2)+v2(m)-1. Frobenius fixed-point count gcd(N0,p-1) follows. Independently checked exponent and modular gradient equations and all valuations for seven parameter triples; finite checks confirm algebra but not the universal ring isomorphism.
